newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended lower again, extending recent declines, but three-month EuroSwiss futures traded on LIFFE ended firmer on the day.
The short end of the market has seen tightness which has boosted money market rates, and also put downward pressure on prices for three-month paper.

Swiss National Bank (SNB) chief economist Georg Rich said that the SNB had added liquidity to the market this morning to counter tightness in the money market, where tomorrow/next rates have risen over two percent. "There is a certain shortage of liquidity and we have tried to counter that," Rich said.
Money market traders blamed technical factors for the tightness in the short end.
A stronger Swiss franc was also likely to have eased upward pressure on short-term Swiss francs.

The longer end of the market remained under pressure as the March confederate bond futures contract fell back to levels last seen in February. The March contract hit a low of 120.20, which was also the session low on February 12.
The trend in the long end was generally in line with declines in German and U.S. bonds.
March Comi medium-term bond steady at 112.00
Mar Euro Swiss francs up four at 98.11.
